label: Zion
meaning: Zion is the name the revelations give to a holy city and a holy people. It can mean a place, a gathered community, or the pure in heart.
discussion: Early revelations tell workers to “seek to bring forth and establish the cause of Zion” (D&C 6:6). D&C 57:1–3 names Independence, Missouri, as the center place for the city. Later sections speak of Zion’s redemption after the Saints were driven out (D&C 101; 105). D&C 97:21 defines Zion as “the pure in heart.”

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Zion

label: Stake
meaning: A stake is a regional church unit that supports Zion. The word comes from the tent stakes that hold up a tent.
discussion: D&C 82:13–14 calls Kirtland “a stake to Zion” and says Zion’s stakes must be strengthened. D&C 101:21 says new gathering places “shall be called stakes, for the curtains or the strength of Zion.” By D&C 124 a stake at Nauvoo has its own president and high council.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Stake

label: Bishop
meaning: A bishop is a church officer who cares for the poor and manages church property. The bishopric is the office or the group that holds it.
discussion: Edward Partridge is called as the first bishop in D&C 41:9. Under D&C 42:30–34 members consecrate property before the bishop, who keeps the surplus for the needy. D&C 107:68–72 says the bishop administers “temporal things” and acts as “a judge in Israel.”

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Bishop

label: Elder
meaning: An elder is an office in the Melchizedek Priesthood. In the D&C the elders are the main traveling preachers and local leaders.
discussion: D&C 20:38–45 lists an elder’s duties: to baptize, ordain, give the Holy Ghost, and lead meetings. It also says “an apostle is an elder.” Many revelations send pairs of elders to preach, as in D&C 52. D&C 107:7 places the office under the Melchizedek Priesthood.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Elder

label: High priest
meaning: A high priest is an office in the Melchizedek Priesthood. High priests could preside, serve as bishops, and sit on high councils.
discussion: The first high priests in the restored church were ordained in June 1831. D&C 68:15–19 says bishops are to be chosen from worthy high priests. D&C 102:1 forms a high council of twelve high priests. D&C 107:53 also calls Adam’s righteous descendants high priests.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: High Priest

label: Priest
meaning: In the D&C a priest is usually an office in the Aaronic Priesthood. Priests may baptize and administer the sacrament.
discussion: D&C 20:46–52 lists a priest’s duties: to preach, baptize, administer the sacrament, and visit members’ homes. D&C 107:87 sets a president over forty-eight priests. The word also appears in other senses, such as “kings and priests” in D&C 76:56. In “high priest” it names a different office.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Priest, Aaronic Priesthood

label: Teacher
meaning: A teacher is an office in the Aaronic Priesthood. Teachers watch over church members and strengthen them.
discussion: D&C 20:53–59 says the teacher must “watch over the church always” and prevent strife among members. Teachers may not baptize or administer the sacrament (D&C 20:58). D&C 84:111 calls teachers and deacons “standing ministers” for local members. In D&C 88:128 “teacher” instead means the presiding instructor of the school of the prophets.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Teacher, Aaronic Priesthood

label: Deacon
meaning: A deacon is the first office in the Aaronic Priesthood. Deacons assist teachers and other officers.
discussion: D&C 20:57–59 says deacons assist teachers and may warn, exhort, and teach. They may not baptize or administer the sacrament. D&C 107:85 sets a president over twelve deacons.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Deacon

label: Aaronic Priesthood
meaning: The Aaronic Priesthood is the lesser of the two priesthoods named in the D&C. It is named after Aaron, the brother of Moses.
discussion: D&C 13 records the words Joseph Smith reported John the Baptist spoke when conferring the “Priesthood of Aaron” in 1829. D&C 107:13–14 explains the name and calls it the lesser priesthood. D&C 107:20 says it holds “the keys of the ministering of angels” and outward ordinances such as baptism.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Aaronic Priesthood

label: Melchizedek Priesthood
meaning: The Melchizedek Priesthood is the higher of the two priesthoods named in the D&C. The revelations also call it the High Priesthood.
discussion: D&C 107:2–4 says it is named after Melchizedek, an ancient high priest, to avoid overusing God’s name. D&C 107:18–19 says it holds the keys of “all the spiritual blessings of the church.” D&C 84:6–17 traces a line of this priesthood back through Moses to Adam.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Melchizedek Priesthood

label: Keys
meaning: In the D&C “keys” means the right to lead and direct a work of God. It is about authority, not physical keys.
discussion: D&C 13:1 says the Aaronic Priesthood holds “the keys of the ministering of angels.” In D&C 110:11–16 Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery reported that Moses, Elias, and Elijah gave them keys. D&C 81:2 says the keys of the kingdom belong to the Presidency of the High Priesthood.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Keys of the Priesthood

label: Consecration
meaning: To consecrate is to dedicate something to God. In the D&C it often means giving property to the church for the poor and for building Zion.
discussion: D&C 42:30–34 tells members to consecrate their property before the bishop “with a covenant and a deed.” Each member then received a stewardship, and the surplus went to the storehouse. The word is also used more broadly, for a consecrated land or house (D&C 57:1; 109:12).

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Consecrate, Law of Consecration
Church History Topics: Consecration and Stewardship

label: Stewardship
meaning: A steward manages what belongs to someone else. In the D&C a stewardship is a portion of property or duty that a person must account for.
discussion: D&C 42:32 makes each member “a steward over his own property” after consecration. D&C 72:3 says every steward must render an account. D&C 104:11–13 divides the united firm’s property into stewardships and says God makes “every man accountable, as a steward over earthly blessings.”

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Steward, Stewardship
Church History Topics: Consecration and Stewardship

label: Storehouse
meaning: The storehouse held goods and funds that the bishop used to care for the poor.
discussion: D&C 42:34 says the surplus from consecration “shall be kept in my storehouse” for the poor and needy. D&C 72:10 makes keeping the storehouse part of a bishop’s work. D&C 83:5–6 says widows and orphans have a claim on the storehouse.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Storehouse

label: Tithing
meaning: Tithing means giving a tenth. In D&C 119 it means surplus property first, then one-tenth of yearly “interest.”
discussion: D&C 64:23 calls the present “a day for the tithing of my people.” D&C 119:1–4, given in 1838, asks for surplus property and then one-tenth of interest annually. D&C 120 then names a council to decide how tithing is spent.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Tithes, Tithing
Church History Topics: Tithing

label: Endowment
meaning: To be endowed is to be given a gift. In the D&C the endowment is a promised gift of “power from on high.”
discussion: D&C 38:32 tells the Saints to go to Ohio, where they would “be endowed with power from on high.” D&C 95:8 and 105:33 tie this promise to the house of the Lord in Kirtland. D&C 110:9 links the endowment to that temple’s dedication in 1836.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Endowment

label: Sealing
meaning: To seal is to bind or confirm with authority. In the D&C sealing power binds something on earth so it is also bound in heaven.
discussion: D&C 128:8–9 describes power by which “whatsoever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven.” D&C 124:124 gives Hyrum Smith “the sealing blessings” of the church. D&C 132 applies sealing to marriage. The word “sealed” is not linked, because it often has other meanings, such as a sealed book.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Seal, Sealing

label: Celestial
meaning: Celestial means heavenly. In the D&C it names the highest of three kingdoms of glory after the resurrection.
discussion: In D&C 76:50–70 Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon reported seeing those who inherit celestial glory, compared to the sun. D&C 88:22 says one must abide a celestial law to receive a celestial glory. D&C 131:1 says the celestial glory has three heavens or degrees.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Celestial Glory

label: Terrestrial
meaning: Terrestrial means earthly. In the D&C it names the middle of three kingdoms of glory.
discussion: D&C 76:71–80 describes the terrestrial world, whose glory is compared to the moon. Verse 79 says its people were “not valiant in the testimony of Jesus.” D&C 88:23 ties terrestrial glory to a terrestrial law.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Terrestrial Glory

label: Telestial
meaning: Telestial is a word coined in the D&C. It names the lowest of three kingdoms of glory.
discussion: D&C 76:81–112 describes telestial glory, compared to the stars. Verse 82 says its people “received not the gospel of Christ.” D&C 88:24 says those who cannot abide even a telestial law inherit no kingdom of glory.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Telestial Glory

label: Urim and Thummim
meaning: The Urim and Thummim was an instrument for receiving revelation. Joseph Smith said he used it to translate the Book of Mormon.
discussion: D&C 10:1 says Joseph translated “by the means of the Urim and Thummim.” D&C 17:1 promises the Three Witnesses a view of it along with the plates. D&C 130:8–10 extends the idea, calling the place where God resides “a great Urim and Thummim.”

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Urim and Thummim
Church History Topics: Seer Stones

label: Seer
meaning: A seer is a person who sees what others cannot, by God’s power. The D&C uses the title for the church president.
discussion: D&C 21:1 says Joseph Smith shall be called “a seer, a translator, a prophet.” D&C 107:92 says the president of the High Priesthood is to be a seer and revelator. D&C 124:94 extends the title to Hyrum Smith.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Seer

label: Lamanites
meaning: The Lamanites are a people in the Book of Mormon. Early church members applied the name to Native Americans.
discussion: D&C 3:18–20 says the Book of Mormon was preserved so the Lamanites could know the promises of the Lord. D&C 28:8 and 32:2 send Oliver Cowdery and others on a mission to the Lamanites in 1830. That mission led west to Missouri, near the later site of Zion.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Lamanites

label: Gathering
meaning: The gathering means bringing believers together into one place or people. The D&C links it to the ancient promise to gather Israel.
discussion: D&C 29:7–8 calls the elders to bring about “the gathering of mine elect” to one place. D&C 57:1 names Missouri as the land “for the gathering of the saints.” In D&C 110:11 Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery reported receiving “the keys of the gathering of Israel” from Moses.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Gathering of Israel

label: School of the Prophets
meaning: The school of the prophets was a class for church leaders in Kirtland, Ohio. It began in early 1833.
discussion: D&C 88:127–141 sets rules for the school, including how members greet one another. D&C 90:7 gives its keys to the First Presidency. D&C 95:10 rebukes contention that arose in the school. The Word of Wisdom (D&C 89) was first given to the school’s members.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: School of the Prophets
Church History Topics: School of the Prophets

label: Word of Wisdom
meaning: The Word of Wisdom is the title of D&C 89, a revelation about food, drink, and health.
discussion: D&C 89 was given in February 1833 for the high priests meeting in Kirtland. Verse 2 says it came “not by commandment or constraint.” It advises against wine, strong drink, tobacco, and hot drinks, and praises grain and fruit. Verses 18–21 promise health and wisdom to those who keep it. In D&C 46:17 “word of wisdom” means a spiritual gift instead, so only the title in D&C 89:1 is linked.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Word of Wisdom

label: Conference
meaning: A conference was a meeting of church members and officers to do church business.
discussion: D&C 20:61–62 tells the elders to meet in conference every three months. D&C 28:10 says Joseph Smith would preside at a coming conference in Fayette. D&C 73:2 and other revelations send elders out “by the voice of the conference.”

label: High council
meaning: A high council is a body of twelve high priests who help govern the church and judge serious disputes.
discussion: D&C 102 records the organization of the first high council in Kirtland in February 1834. Verse 2 says it was formed to settle difficulties that local councils could not. D&C 107:33 calls the Twelve a “Traveling Presiding High Council.”

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: High Council

label: First Presidency
meaning: The First Presidency is the church’s highest governing council. It is made up of the president and his counselors.
discussion: D&C 81:2 and 90:6 describe Joseph Smith and his counselors as holding the keys of the kingdom. D&C 107:22 says three presiding high priests form the quorum of the presidency. D&C 120:1 includes the First Presidency in the council over tithing funds.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: First Presidency

label: The Twelve (Quorum of the Twelve Apostles)
meaning: The Twelve are twelve apostles called as special witnesses of Christ. They form a quorum that travels to lead the church abroad.
discussion: D&C 18:27–37, given in 1829, tells Oliver Cowdery and David Whitmer to seek out the Twelve. The first quorum was chosen in 1835. D&C 107:23–24 says the Twelve are “special witnesses” equal in authority to the First Presidency. D&C 112 instructs Thomas B. Marsh and the Twelve.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Apostle

label: Seventy
meaning: The Seventy are a priesthood office of traveling preachers. They are organized in groups of seventy men.
discussion: D&C 107:25–26 calls the Seventy “especial witnesses unto the Gentiles” and forms them into a quorum. D&C 107:93–97 says seven presidents preside over them. D&C 124:138 names presidents over “the quorum of seventies.” Lowercase “seventy” is not linked because D&C 98:40 uses it as a number.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Seventy

label: Patriarch
meaning: A patriarch is a father figure who gives blessings. In the D&C a church patriarch gives patriarchal blessings to members.
discussion: D&C 124:91–92 gives Hyrum Smith the office of patriarch, held earlier by his father, Joseph Smith Sr. Hyrum was to “hold the keys of the patriarchal blessings” of the church. D&C 135:1 calls him “Hyrum Smith the Patriarch.”

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Patriarch, Patriarchal
Church History Topics: Patriarchal Blessings

label: Ordinance
meaning: An ordinance is a sacred rite done with authority, such as baptism. It can also mean a rule or law.
discussion: D&C 1:15 accuses people of having “strayed from mine ordinances.” D&C 84:20–21 says the power of godliness is shown in the ordinances of the priesthood. D&C 124 and 128 apply the word to temple rites, including baptism for the dead.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Ordinances

label: Baptism for the dead
meaning: Baptism for the dead is a baptism a living person receives on behalf of someone who has died.
discussion: Joseph Smith began teaching the practice in Nauvoo in 1840. D&C 124:29–33 says it belongs in a temple and commands the Saints to build one. D&C 127 and 128 are letters requiring a recorder to witness each baptism. D&C 128:18 says the living and the dead cannot be made perfect without each other.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Salvation for the Dead
Church History Topics: Baptism for the Dead

label: Adam-ondi-Ahman
meaning: Adam-ondi-Ahman is a name from the D&C. It names the land where Adam lived and a settlement in Daviess County, Missouri.
discussion: D&C 107:53–56 says Adam gathered his righteous descendants in “the valley of Adam-ondi-Ahman” to bless them. D&C 116:1, from 1838, says Spring Hill, Missouri, was named Adam-ondi-Ahman. That verse says it is where Adam “shall come to visit his people.”

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Adam-ondi-Ahman

label: The Ohio
meaning: “The Ohio” was an early name for the state of Ohio and its region. Kirtland, Ohio, became church headquarters in 1831.
discussion: D&C 37:1–3 tells the church in New York to “assemble together at the Ohio.” D&C 38:32 promises that in Ohio the Saints would receive God’s law and be “endowed with power.” D&C 39:15 promises a blessing to those who gather there.

related.label: Church History Topics: Kirtland, Ohio

label: Gentiles
meaning: In the Bible, Gentiles are people who are not Israelites. Early church members often counted themselves among the Gentiles.
discussion: D&C 45:28–30 speaks of “the times of the Gentiles” and the gospel coming to them. D&C 107:25 and 107:97 send the Seventy to the Gentiles first, then to the Jews. In D&C 109:60 Joseph Smith’s dedicatory prayer describes the Saints as “identified with the Gentiles.”

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Gentiles

label: Sons of perdition
meaning: Perdition means loss or ruin. The D&C uses “sons of perdition” for those who deny God after knowing his power.
discussion: D&C 76:25–26 says Lucifer was called Perdition after his fall. D&C 76:31–35 describes those who knew God’s power and then denied it. Verses 43–44 say all others are saved except these “sons of perdition.”

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Sons of Perdition
Guide to the Scriptures: Perdition

label: Spirit world
meaning: The spirit world is the place where the spirits of the dead wait for the resurrection.
discussion: D&C 138 records a vision Joseph F. Smith reported in 1918. In verses 18–23 he saw Christ visit the righteous dead. Verses 28–37 say Christ organized messengers to teach “the spirits in prison.” Verse 57 says faithful elders keep preaching there after death.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Spirit World

label: New and everlasting covenant
meaning: The new and everlasting covenant means the fulness of the gospel and its covenants. In D&C 131 and 132 it refers especially to eternal marriage.
discussion: D&C 131:1–4 says entering this order of the priesthood is needed for the highest degree of celestial glory. D&C 132:6–7 says the covenant was instituted for the fulness of God’s glory. D&C 132:19 joins it to marriages sealed by the Holy Spirit of promise. The same section also gave the revelation on plural marriage.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: New and Everlasting Covenant

label: Comforter
meaning: The Comforter is a title for the Holy Ghost, taken from the Gospel of John.
discussion: D&C 36:2 promises that Edward Partridge will receive “the Holy Ghost, even the Comforter.” D&C 42:17 says the Comforter “knoweth all things.” D&C 88:3–4 speaks of “another Comforter,” called the Holy Spirit of promise.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Comforter

label: Holy Spirit of promise
meaning: The Holy Spirit of promise is the Holy Ghost acting to confirm covenants and blessings as valid.
discussion: D&C 76:53 says those in celestial glory are “sealed by the Holy Spirit of promise.” D&C 132:7 says covenants not sealed in this way end at death. D&C 88:3–4 links this Spirit to the promise of eternal life.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Holy Spirit of Promise

label: Book of Commandments
meaning: The Book of Commandments was the first planned book of Joseph Smith’s revelations. Its printing in Missouri stopped in 1833.
discussion: Church leaders agreed to publish the revelations at a November 1831 conference. D&C 1 was given as the preface to that book. In D&C 67:6 the revelation challenges critics to write something like “the least” of its revelations. A mob destroyed the press in Independence in July 1833 before the book was finished.

related.label: Church History Topics: Book of Commandments

label: Doctrine and Covenants
meaning: The Doctrine and Covenants is a book of Joseph Smith’s revelations and later additions. It was first published in Kirtland in 1835.
discussion: D&C 124:141 already refers to “the book of Doctrine and Covenants” for instructions on the bishopric. D&C 135:3 and 135:6 list it among the works Joseph Smith brought forth. Later editions added sections, such as D&C 138 in 1981.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Doctrine and Covenants

label: New Jerusalem
meaning: The New Jerusalem is a holy city to be built in the last days. The D&C places it in America and links it with Zion.
discussion: D&C 42:9 promises the city will be revealed in time. D&C 45:66–67 calls it “a land of peace, a city of refuge,” and says it will be called Zion. D&C 84:2–4 says the city and its temple will be built in western Missouri.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: New Jerusalem

label: Elias
meaning: Elias is the Greek form of the name Elijah. In the D&C it can name a person, a role of forerunner, or a messenger who restores.
discussion: D&C 27:6–7 speaks of Elias as one who holds keys to restore all things. D&C 77:14 reads a passage in Revelation as describing an Elias who gathers Israel. In D&C 110:12, Elias and Elijah appear separately in the same vision.

related.label: Guide to the Scriptures: Elias
